request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Intersect governance coordination, ecosystem coordination, technical stewardship, incident response, release coordination, and management of critical unowned processes for June 2026 to June 2027.

claims.claim: Intersect requests 25,400,000 ADA for its core operating model from June 2026 to June 2027.
The proposal says Intersect's overall ask has decreased from $7.875M last year to $6.35M this year while preserving critical functions.
Intersect says it supports Cardano through committees and working groups, core Haskell repository stewardship, upgrades, incident response, and community-approved initiative administration.
Intersect claims it has already coordinated two network upgrades, is preparing for a third, and led ecosystem coordination during the November 2025 chain partition incident.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to voting documentation and audited results.
The proposal states the withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission and links to the relevant governance action.
Intersect discloses 22,385,000 ADA in prior treasury funding to Intersect and its committees within the past 24 months across three listed governance actions.
Independent audits and assurance for this proposal will be provided by Appold, with possible reviews of deliverables, controls, spend validation, and milestone evidence.

The proposal states funds will be managed through Sundae Labs smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, external oversight entities, multisignature-like approval thresholds, and audit references for the contract framework.
A dashboard at treasury.sundae.fi is provided for community tracking and on-chain auditability of the withdrawn ADA.

summary: The document requests 25,400,000 ADA for Intersect's 2026-2027 operating, governance coordination, technical stewardship, incident response, and critical-process functions, with budget breakdowns, prior-funding disclosure, voting and NCL references, and smart-contract management details.
